Though the appeal is listed for Admission, with the consent of learned counsel for both the parties,
the same is taken up for final disposal.

2. The insurer is in appeal challenging the judgment and award, dated 27.11.2021, passed in M.V.C.
No.279/2018 by the Civil Judge (Sr. Dn.) and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Koppal,
(for short, 'the Tribunal') on the ground of Tribunal failing to consider the contributory negligence and also on the ground of grant of excessive compensation.
3.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Koppal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The claimants - wife, children and mother of the deceased K.Suresh, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation for the accidental death of deceased K.Suresh in a road traffic accident that occurred on 18.01.2018 involving Motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-37/X-2690 and a lorry bearing registration No.MH-16/Q-7827.
They claimed that the NC: 2023:KHC-D:7393-DB deceased was aged 40 years as on the date of the accident, he was in hotel business and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
4. On issuance of notice, respondents No.1 and 2 appeared before the Tribunal.
Respondent No.2-insurer filed its written statement.

Respondent No2-insurer, in its written statement, denied the claim petition averments and contended that respondent No.1, the owner of the lorry, was not having a valid and effective driving licence with necessary endorsement to drive the lorry.
It also contended that the lorry was being plied without having a valid permit and beyond the area of permit and hence there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy.

It also contended that the lorry was parked on the extreme left side of the road by switching on its signal lights and indicators,
but the accident occurred solely due to the negligence of the deceased rider of the motorcycle.
It is stated that if the deceased was cautious in riding the motorcycle, he could have easily passed over the parked NC: 2023:KHC-D:7393-DB lorry.
It is also stated that the road on which the lorry was parked is a Four-lane National Highway having a divider and as such there was no occasion of glaring of the headlights of the oncoming vehicles.
Therefore, it was contended that the deceased K.Suresh was solely responsible for the accident and not respondent No.1.
It is also stated that as the Police had filed charge sheet both against the deceased rider of the motor cycle as well as the driver of the lorry, it is a case of contributory negligence.
Thus, the insurer prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.

sentences.text: To prove their case, the claimants examined claimant No.1, the wife of the deceased, as P.W.1 and also examined one more witness as P.W.2, and got marked thirteen documents as Ex.P.1 to P.13.
The respondent- insurer examined its Officer as R.W.1 and got marked four documents as Exs.R.1 to R.4.

The Tribunal, on scrutiny of the material on record, awarded total compensation of Rs.23,70,840/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, under the following heads:
NC: 2023:KHC-D:7393-DB 1 Loss of Dependency Rs. 22,20,840/- 2
Towards loss of estate Rs. 15,000/- 3 Towards consortium Rs. 1,20,000/- 4 Towards Funeral expenses Rs. 15,000/-

TOTAL Rs. 23,70,840/-
While awarding the above compensation, the Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.11,750/- per month added 40% of the assessed income towards future prospects, adopted multiplier '15', and deducted 1/4th of the assessed income towards personal expenses of the deceased.
The Tribunal has also awarded a sum of Rs.1,20,000/- towards loss of consortium.

6. Heard learned counsel Smt. Preethi Shashank for the appellant-insurer, learned counsel M.Amare Gouda for claimants/respondents No.1, 2 & 4, and learned counsel, Sri. D.V.Pattar for respondent No.5, the owner of the lorry.
Perused the appeal papers and Trial Court records.

7. Learned counsel Smt. Preethi Shashank, for the appellant would submit that the Tribunal committed a grave error in not considering the contributory negligence NC: 2023:KHC-D:7393-DB as the rider of the motorcycle was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident.

She contends that when the chargesheet is filed against both, the deceased rider of the motorcycle and the driver of the lorry, the Tribunal is not justified in not considering the contention of the appellant with regard to contributory negligence.

Further, the learned counsel would submit that the lorry was parked on the extreme left side of the road with indicators and signals, but the deceased rider of the motorcycle without noticing the same dashed to the stationed lorry which resulted in his death;
there was sufficient way on the right side of the road to go past the lorry as it was parked on the left side of the Highway and there was 20 feet wide road on the right side; there was no question of the rider of the motor cycle getting glared by the opposite direction high beam vehicle as the road on which the accident occurred was National Highway; the damage caused to the motorcycle would indicate that the rider of the motor cycle was rash and negligent in riding the motor cycle.
Thus, on NC: 2023:KHC-D:7393-DB the above grounds, she prays for considering and fixing the contributory negligence on the rider of the motorcycle.

8. Learned counsel for the appellant-insurer would also submit that the insurer had also contended that the owner of the lorry had no valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident to drive the lorry and in that regard, the insurer had issued notice to the respondent No.1 (before the Tribunal) to produce the licence.

It is submitted that as respondent No1. has not produced the driving licence, it is to be presumed that respondent No.1 had no licence to drive the lorry and the insurer would not be liable to indemnify respondent No.1-owner of the lorry.

Referring to the decision of the National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi NC: 2023:KHC-D:7393-DB & Others1, learned counsel would submit that the decision makes it clear that the Tribunal could add 40% of the assessed income towards future prospects if the deceased was aged below 40 years, and if the deceased was aged 40 years, the claimants would be entitled for adding of 25% of the assessed income towards future prospects.

10.

Per contra, Sri. M.Amaregouda, learned counsel for the respondents/claimants would submit that the Tribunal is right in holding that the driver of the lorry is solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident since the lorry was parked on the middle of the road.
Therefore, he justifies the finding of the Tribunal.
Learned counsel would submit that the insurance company has failed to examine the driver of the lorry who would have been the best witness to narrate the incident.

Further, he would AIR 2017 SC 5157 - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7393-DB submit that the lorry was parked on the middle of the highway without indicators and parking lights, therefore, the driver of the lorry is solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident.

11. With regard to the quantum of compensation, learned counsel for the respondents/claimants would submit that since the deceased was aged 40 years, the claimants would be entitled for adding of 40% of the assessed income towards future prospects.

Further, the learned counsel would submit that the Tribunal has failed to award a sum of Rs.40,000/- each to all the claimants in terms of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., Vs.
Nanu Ram and Others 2.

Thus,
he prays for dismissal of the appeal filed by the insurer.

On hearing the learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the appeal papers including the Trial Court records, the following points would arise for consideration:
i) Whether the Tribunal is justified in coming to the conclusion that the accident occurred solely due to the negligence of the driver of the lorry and saddling the liability on the insurer of the lorry?
The Divisional Manager vs Smt. Jadiyamma K W/O. Suresh K on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144870409/
5 ii) Whether the Tribunal committed an error in granting 40% of the assessed income towards future prospects?
13.

The answers to the above points would be in the affirmative and negative respectively for the following reasons:
a) The accident that that occurred on 18.01.2018 involving Motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-37/X- 2690 and a lorry bearing registration No.MH-16/Q- 7827 and the resultant death of K.Suresh is not in dispute in this appeal.
- 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7393-DB b)
The insurer mainly contends that the Tribunal failed to consider the contention of the insurer with regard to the contributory negligence.
Admittedly, the insured lorry was parked on the National Highway and the rider of the motorcycle dashed to the parked lorry from the hind side which resulted in his death.
On a perusal of the charge sheet, which contains the spot sketch, it is clear that the lorry was parked almost on the middle of the road.
There was ten feet space left on the left side and 15 feet space on the right side of the lorry.
The rider of the motorcycle was coming from Kushtagi to Hospet and the offending lorry, which was also moving from Kushtagi to Hospet, was parked almost on the middle of the National Highway.
P.W.2 is the complainant and also an eyewitnesses to the incident.
P.W.2 has deposed that the lorry was parked on the middle of the road and the lorry was not visible to the glaring light of the vehicles coming from the opposite direction.
P.W.2 has also deposed that he has seen the accident and the accident occurred due to the - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7393-DB negligence of the driver in parking the lorry on the middle of the road.

In his cross-examination, P.W.2 has stated that the accident has taken place at 8.00 p.m. on the National Highway and he has seen the occurrence of the accident, but nothing is elicited in favour of the insurer.
P.W.2 has further stated that lorry was parked without indicators and the lorry was parked in the middle of the road.
When the evidence of P.W.2, along with the sketch at Ex.P.5, is considered, the conclusion arrived at by the Tribunal is proper and correct.
The accident had occurred solely due to parking of the lorry in the middle of the road without indicators by respondent No.1.

Though the chargesheet is filed against the deceased rider of the motorcycle and also against the driver of the lorry, the same cannot be a ground to say that the deceased was also responsible for the occurrence of the accident.

Moreover, it is to be noted that the insurer has not examined the driver of the lorry who would have been the right person to depose with regard to - 14 - The Divisional Manager vs Smt. Jadiyamma K W/O. Suresh K on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144870409/
6 NC: 2023:KHC-D:7393-DB parking of the lorry on the middle of the road as well the occurrence of the accident.

sentences.text: Thus, the contention of the insurer with regard to the contributory negligence has no merit and it is accordingly, rejected.

c) With regard to the contention that respondent No.1- driver of the lorry had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the lorry, the insurer had produced and marked Ex.P.3 which is the office copy of the legal notice issued to respondent No.1.
The acknowledgment for having served the notice is not placed on record though the postal receipt is placed on record.
Moreover, the insurer has failed to summon either the RTO or the driver of the lorry.
Though the insurer contended that the 1st respondent has no licence to driver the lorry, it has failed to prove the same.

d) The income of the deceased assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.11,750/- per month, the multiplier '15'
adopted by the Tribunal, and the deduction of 1/4th of the - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7393-DB assessed income towards personal expenses of the deceased are proper and correct and the same requires no interference.
e) The Tribunal committed a grave error in adding 40% of the assessed income towards future prospects.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra) has made it clear that the claimants would be entitled for adding 40% of the assessed income towards future prospects if the deceased was self- employed and aged below 40 years.
In the instant case, the deceased was aged 40 years and not below 40 years.
Therefore, the claimants would be entitled for adding of 25% of the assessed income towards future prospects.

Thus, the claimants would be entitled for modified compensation of Rs.19,82,812/- [Rs.11,750 Add Rs.2,937.50 ps. (25% of Rs.11,750/-) = Rs.14,687.50 x 12 x 15 less 1/4th towards personal expenses] under the head 'loss of dependency'.
- 16 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7393-DB f)

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.15,000/- each towards 'loss of estate' and 'funeral expenses' and a sum of Rs.40,000/- towards 'loss of consortium' to claimant No.1 i.e, the wife of the deceased, which is in accordance with the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi's case (supra).
g) The Tribunal taking note of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., (supra) has rightly awarded a sum of Rs.40,000/- to claimants No.2 and 3, the minor children of the deceased, towards loss of parental consortium.

In view of the above decision,
the parents of the deceased would also be entitled for compensation towards loss of filial consortium.
Therefore, in the instant case, claimant No.4 being the mother of the deceased would also be entitled for a sum of Rs.40,000/- towards 'loss of filial consortium'.

Thus, the claimants would be entitled for modified compensation on the following heads:
1 Loss of Dependency Rs. 19,82,812/- 2
Towards loss of estate Rs. 15,000/- 3

Towards consortium (to claimants Rs. 1,60,000/-
No.1 to 4 at Rs.40,000/- each)
4 Towards Funeral expenses Rs. 15,000/-

TOTAL Rs. 21,72,812/-
Thus, the claimants would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.21,72,812/- as against Rs.23,70,840/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

15. Hence, we pass the following:
ORDER a) The appeal is allowed in part to the extent of reducing the compensation towards future prospects from 40% to 25% of the assessed income.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified reducing the compensation from Rs.23,70,840/- to Rs.21,72,812/-.
The modified compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till date of realization.

- 18 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7393-DB c) The appellant-Insurance Company shall deposit the compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
d) Apportionment, deposit and disbursement of the modified compensation shall be made as per the award of the Tribunal.
e) Draw modified award accordingly.
Registry to transmit the records to the Tribunal forthwith.
